_about: English for every player-visible Portuguese string of Penumbra and the Castle of Shadows (2010), read by game/render/Localization. Keys are the original's text in UTF-8 (the game holds it as cp1252 bytes; the loader converts). Line breaks are kept where the original has them, and lines are kept about as long as the Portuguese, because every text is drawn at a fixed place (menu panel at x=652, 391 px wide; help messages at (10,70) in Arial 30; lore signs in Arial Narrow 16). Lookup trims the text's leading and trailing whitespace and puts it back around the English, so keys carry none. Keys starting with '_' are notes. Sources: extracted/app/*.as (DrawText, shadowText, showData, addMessage, Switch labels), data.enml (global.story01-04, soldados, fun, comboTip, bridge, annoying, flyingWall, portalToCastle, warning, nights, wisdom, arena1-6), scenes/*.esc (help signs' 'message', arena thumbnails' 'title'). Not listed: the TESTING-only debug overlays ('FPS: ', 'NPCs: ', controlCharacters.as:206, setupScene.as:329), which the shipped build never compiled.
_languages: ENHANCEMENT E24: the languages the game is drawn in, in the options screen's order (the Magic Rampage Companion app's picker order), each named in its own script - the same in every language. The ids are render/Languages.hpp's (settings.json, --lang, strings/<id>.json, images/<id>/); rtl: right to left. Every language but English and Portuguese has its own file, strings/<id>.json, keyed by the Portuguese as this file is (render/Localization.hpp).

•2 players:
 If a joystick is plugged in,
 the main character gains
 the power to summon a
 creature that can be controlled
 by the 2nd player.

 To summon the creature, just
 press START on the 2nd controller.

 The summoning spell costs 50 mana
 and one life, but it lets 2
 players fight side by side.

 Only player 1 can pick up
 checkpoints and finish a level.

strings.Penumbra não é um bom lugar\npara se viv:
Penumbra is no place to
make a life. When the mist
lifts, the storm rolls in.

Ages ago, a mighty sorcerer
seized control of the
gloomy land called Penumbra,
naming himself king of this world.

For centuries, the Order of the
Wizards of Penumbra has sought
to overthrow the tyrant.

After countless years training
in the arts of magic and combat,
you have been chosen by the Order
to go to the Castle of Shadows
of Penumbra and slay the king,
ending a reign that has lasted
for years.

touch._about: ENHANCEMENT E16: the original's control hints - every text it draws that names a key to press - worded for the on-screen touch controls, drawn in place of the original (either language) while they are on (render/Localization SetTouch, from the layer's switch every frame; off, the text is exactly what it always was). Keyed by the original's Portuguese as 'strings' is; whole strings only. The buttons are named by what they show: the arrows at the bottom left (the direction control, left, right and down), the jump, sword, fire and light buttons at the bottom right in two columns of three with the two combo buttons between them (the middle row, E29), the pause button at the top right. Each fits where the original is drawn (the help messages at (10,70) in Arial 30 and at half size under the wizard; the how-to-play panel's 381 px column in Arial Narrow 25, 768 px tall; the lore sign's two lines in Arial Narrow 16), which test_pn_render_hud measures. Not here, on purpose: 'Pressione Alt+Enter...' (menu.as:101: E20 does not draw it on a phone, and a desktop with touch controls still has the keyboard it names); the Versus screen's second paragraph, 'Já há um joystick plugado...' (menu.as:281-283: drawn only with a pad on player 1's index, which the touch controls never give a pad, E22) and the settings blurb (menu.as:151: what the screen sets up, not a key to press); the options' row labels.

images._about: Images with Portuguese baked into their pixels, keyed by the path the original loads (a normal or gloss map is its own entry). 'en' is the English variant's path relative to this file's folder, generated by tools/art/make_english_art.py from the original (same size, mode and layout, so every rectangle the scripts compute still fits); empty means the original is drawn in both languages. Localization::ImageVariant returns it when it exists. 'labels' is what the variant says. entities/gameover.png already reads 'Game Over'.

entities/menu_buttons.png._note: menu.esc's buttons (buttons.ent), 512x512, one label per 512x64 frame; its normal map and gloss map carry the same letters and have their own entries below

entities/normalmaps/menu_nm_buttons.png._note: buttons.ent's <Normal>: the English labels embossed the way the original's are (render/Lighting resolves it)

entities/menu_buttons_gloss.png._note: buttons.ent's <Gloss>: the English label mask, so the highlight (render/Lighting resolves it) does not show the Portuguese letters

entities/gamelogo.png._note: the title on the menu (gamelogo.ent). 'Penumbra' is the original's pixels; the subtitle's hand-cut uncial has no installed match, so the English is Matura MT Script Capitals at the original's x-height and span - a judgement call: empty 'en' to keep the Portuguese subtitle

interface/arrow_button.png._note: the video options screen's back button (videoModes.as:81, DrawSprite); 'Back' in Matura MT Script Capitals, as the logo

interface/input_options1.png._note: g_controls' first option: keyboard for player 1, joystick for player 2 (switch.as:98, DrawSprite)
